title: A chat app with custom events
idea: A chat room is a hub that emits events you name yourself: `join`, `message`, `leave`. Users listen to the hub, never to each other.

analogy.text: A group chat. You post once to the group, and the app delivers it to every member's phone.
analogy.breaks: Here all users live in one program; real chats cross a network.

points: A class can extend `EventEmitter`, so the room has its own methods and events.
`say` only emits `message`; the room never calls a user directly.
`join` adds the user's listener and returns a function that removes it with `off`.
Events are not replayed: only listeners present at `emit` time hear them.

messages.label: join('Ben')
messages.note: Ben joins the same way. The room now holds two `message` listeners.

messages.label: say('Ana', 'hi Ben')
messages.note: `say` emits one `message` event. Ana does not know who is listening.

messages.label: message from Ana
messages.note: Ben's listener runs and prints. Ana's own listener skips her message.

messages.label: say('Ben', 'hi Ana')
messages.note: Ben replies the same way, with one emit.

messages.label: message from Ben
messages.note: Ana's listener runs and prints. Ben's own listener skips his message.

messages.label: leaveBen()
messages.note: The function `join` returned calls `off`, so Ben's listener is gone. One `message` listener remains.

code.title: A chat room on events
code.caption: Add a third user, or call `room.say` after Ben leaves, and predict who sees it.

walk.text: Each user gets an inbox listener. It prints messages from other users, never their own.
Emit `join` so anyone listening can react.
Return a leave function. It removes the exact listener with `off`, then emits `leave`.
`say` emits one `message` event with the sender and the text.
Create the room and add two listeners that log `join` and `leave`.
Two users join and talk. Ben leaves, so only Ana's listener remains.

pitfalls: Forgetting `off` on leave keeps ghost listeners: they still receive messages and leak memory.
`off` needs the same function you passed to `on`; save it in a variable.
Share event names as constants; a typo like `mesage` silently reaches no listener.

quiz.why: `emit` reaches only listeners that exist at that moment. `hello` was emitted before anyone listened, so it is lost.

takeaway: One hub, custom events: a new feature is often one more listener.

starters: How would I keep message history for people who join late?
Could this chat work between two computers?
When should I use events instead of plain function calls?
